messages:
anna_cs: FYI customer AcmePay is reporting 504s and high p95s for hosted inference since ~09:12 UTC. They say it started right after a billing webhook error. Can we triage?
sara_support: thanks — can you paste a sample request/trace and tenant id? also any client-side retry spikes?
acme_dev: tenant=acme-501, getting 504s on /v1/generate. Client sees immediate retry bursts, ~3 retries per call. Example curl: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-XXXX' -d '{"prompt":"<~2k tokens>"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate`
mike_oncall: pinging runtime oncall. is this auth 401 or gateway 504?
acme_dev: header shows 504 gateway, but logs from client show intermittent 502/500 from auth service earlier. Billing console shows webhook retries failing between 09:10-09:14 (502).
jin_runtime: grabbing logs. I see auth-service returned 502->500 for a bunch of tokens from acme-501 around 1719123100-1719123340. Gateway started queuing requests waiting for auth validation. Continuous-batcher backlog grows when auth latencies go up because requests with long seq lengths hold the batch slot.
sara_support: do we have queue metrics? what hit the limits?
jin_runtime: logs: `request_queue.depth: spike 0->52 (limit=50)`, `continuous_batcher.latency.p95: 840ms -> 2.1s`, `kvcache.warmup.ms: 120 -> 980` for large seq requests. Also saw `auth-client timeout` retries adding to in-flight.
mike_oncall: that depth > limit explains tail timeouts. looks like billing webhook flaked -> auth slow -> requests stacked up -> long-seq jobs prevented enqueue progress.
acme_dev: how do we mitigate now? customers are getting 504s and the support ticket is sticky.
jin_runtime: immediate mitigations: 1) apply per-tenant in-flight cap lower than global limit for acme-501 2) route acme to smaller model variant (fewer tokens / faster) 3) enable auth-service short-circuit: if billing check fails with 5xx treat as soft deny 4) drop long-seq requests early with explain response so client can backoff.
mike_oncall: I can apply the per-tenant cap and route to fallback. doing admin API: `POST https://control.redwood.com/admin/tenant/acme-501/config -d '{"inflight_limit":8, "fallback_model":"redwood-small"}'` -> applied.
sara_support: applied and confirmed — p95 for acme dropped from 2.1s -> 420ms within 20s of rule. Some 504s still ramping down. :thumbsup:
jin_runtime: added a temporary rule to reject requests >1500 tokens with a 429 and message to client to chunk (will revert in 2h). Patch shows effect on batching occupancy immediately.
billing-bot: billing webhook retries succeeded at 09:18 UTC; downstream auth-service recovered at ~09:19 UTC.
acme_dev: saw service stabilize, errors dropped to near zero. thanks for fast action.
mike_oncall: root cause summary for postmortem: billing webhook transient 502 caused auth-service timeouts -> gateway queued auth-dependent requests -> continuous batching backlog amplified because some tenants sent very long sequences and client retry amplification increased queue depth -> tail-latency 504s.
jin_runtime: follow-ups: - add circuit-breaker in auth client to fail fast on billing downstream 5xx - enforce per-tenant token-length caps and sensible defaults - surface billing webhook health in runtime routing UI - add an alert for auth-dependent queue depth > 70% of limit and p95 batcher latency > 500ms - consider prewarming kvcache for large-seq tenants during rollout windows.
sara_support: I'll create the support ticket write-up and notify AcmePay CS. anna, pls add billing and infra owners to postmortem.
anna_cs: on it — I'll include timeline and mitigation commands we ran.
acme_dev: confirmed customer happy with mitigation, will follow our new recommended token caps. thanks all. :heart:
